why: The stuffed animal is now clearly in the downward camera - black and white plush with a yellow beak, sitting on the blue-taped mat inside the black table frame. It centres 265 px right and 220 px below frame centre, and since image-up is my forward direction (confirmed by my own sideways move last step making the ground slide left while the teal tub stayed at frame top), that means it is about 0.36 m to my RIGHT and 0.30 m BEHIND me. The policy has the sideways part right but wants to go forward 0.27 m, which is the wrong sign and would push the target further out of the downward view, and it adds a 47 deg yaw I do not need. Taking a short 0.47 m back-and-right step to put the animal under me, holding altitude at 1.2 m so the downward view keeps it in frame.
